When King Rehoboam threatens violence ('I will chastise you with scorpions') in response to the people's petition, this harsh approach precipitates rebellion and the division of the kingdom. The narrative shows that the elders' counsel for mercy and service ('if you will be a servant to this people...they will be your servants forever') was the preferable leadership approach. Rehoboam's choice of violence-based leadership results in loss of the kingdom's unity—presented as a negative consequence, not a model to emulate. The text documents this as failed leadership rather than exemplary leadership.
